developments.title: Treasury financing estimates resolve the elapsed funding checkpoint
developments.facts: Treasury projects Q4 privately held net marketable borrowing of USD 618 bn, USD 10 bn below August, with unchanged USD 850 bn end-December cash. Excluding the higher opening cash balance, the estimate rises USD 24 bn. Q1 borrowing is projected at USD 800 bn with USD 1 tn end-March cash. November 2 repo acceptance was zero in the morning and USD 2 mn in the afternoon; reverse repo was USD 5.087 bn. The two-year OTC indication is now around 4.61%, slightly above the prior session, so the earlier intraday decline cannot be extended mechanically. November 2 13/26-week bill discount rates were 4.040%/4.150%, bid-to-cover 2.88/2.89. Routine collateral operations and bill awards do not establish QE or exceptional funding stress.

direction.reason: Retained Slight weakening. September consents fell 7.9% and the RBNZ majority’s weak household-demand and wage-transmission rationale still dominates over the regional handover. Strong annual consent growth, export/business pricing resilience, high conditional December hike likelihood, cheaper energy and Chinese support form the strongest opposite case. They make the negative advantage limited rather than a new collapse: stronger majority guidance or a broad regional-demand recovery would defeat it. The new consents actual is separate from tomorrow’s still-unknown jobs and wages. AUD has firmer capacity support, but its technology exposure leaves the equal-grade cross insufficiently clear before RBA.
direction.horizon: Current session to the saved mechanism-specific checkpoint; no automatic continuation beyond it.
